scope: Bedrijfsgeheugen Powerhouse / learning writeback / chat-agent continuity / deduplication
trigger: A repeated user request to borg/log/documenteer the same already-canonicalized recovery learning after PR #1922 had merged and Completion Supervisor evidence had already been updated.
problem: Without an explicit idempotency rule, repeated writeback requests can create duplicate learning records, duplicate documentation, conflicting fingerprints, unnecessary CI/deploy cost, and divergent truth about whether a learning is already canonical.
decision: Treat repeated writeback as reconcile/append against the existing canonical record, not as permission to create a second copy. First prove whether the learning/fingerprint already exists on protected main and in the canonical runtime memory. Only create a new record when there is genuinely new semantic learning; otherwise append fresh evidence to the existing lineage or perform no-op readback confirmation.
required_preflight: search canonical brain/learning for the incident fingerprint and learning_id
search docs/learning and known-error contracts for the same semantic rule
read protected main identity before mutation
read canonical runtime obligation/evidence when the learning is tied to an existing obligation
compare requested writeback with already-recorded semantics before creating files or obligations
reusable_decision_sequence: resolve the semantic fingerprint from the user's request
search existing canonical learning and runtime evidence
if identical semantics already exist and no new evidence exists, do not mutate; return readback proof
if identical semantics exist but new evidence exists, append/reconcile into the existing lineage
if a genuinely new lesson exists, create one new canonical learning linked to the source learning and owner
run the normal protected exact-head gates for repository mutations
after merge, read back protected main and update the existing runtime authority rather than creating a parallel store
